blocks.text: A1-01 · Greetings and presentations
Lesson overview

In this unit, you move from reading to communicating. You will learn the expressions Arabic speakers use to greet each other, introduce themselves and say goodbye in Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), as well as the difference between addressing a man and a woman, which you can hear in every question in Arabic. These are fixed expressions: learn them as complete chunks. You will explore the grammar behind them in later units.

rows: 6–7 hours · one week (week 13 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-01), voice synthesis script, first session with the tutor (30 minutes)
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. healthy and respond to greetings at different times of the day, with the correct matched response;
2. to present yourself by name and ask the name of a man and a woman;
3. ask and tell how you are, choosing ⁧حَالُكَ⁩ or ⁧حَالُكِ⁩ according to who you are before;
4. thank you, apologize, dismiss you;
5. to recognize the formulas of daily use by God's name and to respond adequately;
6. read the transliteration of the volume, which follows the reading "in pause"

0. How to read the Arabic of this volume

From here on Arabic is printed in full vocalization , including the final vowels indicating the function of the word in the sentence (the case endings, which you will study in A1-19). Transliteration follows formal reading with a simple rule:
• Inside the sentence everything is pronounced: ⁧كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟⁩ kayfa ḥāluka? ;
• in pause, i.e. before a punctuation mark or at the end of the stroke, falls the last short vowel and the tanwīn - one/-in: ⁧بِخَيْرٍ⁩ read bi-ḫayr , ⁧السَّلَامُ⁩ read as-salām ; the ⁧ة⁩ read -a;
• Suffix pronouns remain whole (-ka, -ki, -hu, -hā...), because they distinguish the meaning: ⁧حَالُكِ⁩ ḥāluki ;
• tanwīn -an of formulas and adverbs remains -an also in pause: ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ šukran .
In spontaneous speech, many Arabic speakers fail to hear the endings even within the sentence. In your oral productions of A1 It is not a mistake: it is important to speak the word well.

2. The formulas and their answers
In Arabic many greetings have a fixed answer: the same formula is not repeated, it is answered with that paired. Learn them in pairs.

Because that's how it works. The paired formulas are a game of revival: to the "Peace" is answered with peace, to the "Bene" is answered with the "Luce" (light), which is something more. Responding with the right formula indicates that you know the rules of courtesy; repeating the same formula is understandable, but it sounds like a beginner. More words of courtesy. ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ / ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكِ⁩ min faḍlika / min faḍliki Please (to a man/woman) · ⁧آسِف⁩ / ⁧آسِفَة⁩ āsif / āsifa I'm sorry, I'm sorry (said by a man/woman), to whom you respond. ⁧لَا بَأْسَ⁩ lā baʾs It's okay. ⁧نَعَمْ⁩ naʿam "Yes" · ⁧لَا⁩ lā "No" is the name. Titles. ⁧أُسْتَاذ⁩ ustāḏ "Professor" is a teacher, but also a respectable one for an educated man; ⁧أُسْتَاذَة⁩ ustāḏa for a woman. ⁧سَيِّد⁩ Sayyid -- sir -- ⁧سَيِّدَة⁩ Sayyida ... ma'am... are used before the name: ⁧السَّيِّدُ كَرِيم⁩ as-sayyid Karīm . To call someone he puts on ⁧يَا⁩ yā in front of the name or title: ⁧يَا سَلْمَى⁩ yā Salmā , ⁧يَا أُسْتَاذُ⁩ yā ustāḏ .
3. Man or woman: your shape changes

In Arabic, the "tu" has two forms: ⁧أَنْتَ⁩ door for a man and ⁧أَنْتِ⁩ anti for a woman. The same is true of the suffix "your": -ka for a man, -ki for a woman. Every formula addressed to a person therefore changes according to the listener.

rows: What's your name? (Lett. What is your name?

blocks.text: ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ min faḍlika ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكِ⁩ min faḍliki Please

The formulas with -kum, how ⁧السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ • on you • they are plural but are also used with only one person : they are fixed. Instead, the shape changes according to who speaks in ⁧آسِف⁩ / : ⁧آسِفَة⁩ Luca says ⁧آسِف⁩ , Salmā says ⁧آسِفَة⁩ . Without verbs be. In ⁧اِسْمِي لُوكَا⁩ ismī Lūkā My name [is] Luke and in ⁧أَنَا المُدَرِّسَةُ⁩ "I [am] the teacher" is not the verb "to be": at present Arabic does not use it. You'll study it in A1-02; He's imitated the model for now.

blocks.text: 5. Pronunciation

⁧ع⁩ in formulas. ⁧عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ , ⁧عَفْوًا⁩ , ⁧مَعَ⁩ begin or contain ʿayn: it is a full consonant, with the compressed pharynx (L0-07). alaykum without ʿayn is the most recognizable mistake of an Italian. ⁧ح⁩ , ⁧خ⁩ and ⁧ه⁩ . ⁧حَال⁩ and ⁧الحَمْد⁩ have ḥāʾ, deaf African of the faringe, without scrape; ⁧خَيْر⁩ has ḫāʾ, with the scraper at the bottom of the mouth; ⁧أَهْلًا⁩ has hāʾ, a light aspiration. Three different sounds in three formulas you will use every day. Solar letters. ⁧السَّلَام⁩ as-salām and ⁧النُّور⁩ an-nūr assimilate the article; ⁧الخَيْر⁩ al-ḫayr and ⁧الحَمْد⁩ al-ḥamd no (L0-04). The support vowel. In ⁧وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ⁩ the word ⁧عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ ends without vowel and the next begins with an aliif waṣla: To tie them you add a vowel, here u: wa-ʿalaykumu s-salām . It's the same rule of ⁧عَنِ التَّحْقِيقِ⁩ in L0-09. . ⁧الله⁩ The double Allāh It is veiled, darkened [ɫɫ], after a and u: Allāh , šāʾa llāh . After the news is clear: li-llāh in
⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ .
The tanwīn -an. In ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ , ⁧عَفْوًا⁩ , ⁧مَرْحَبًا⁩ the final alif is only the support of tanwīn: you read -an , not -ā Long.

8. Culture and register

The safest greeting. ⁧السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ is understood and used throughout the Arab world, by Muslims and, in many areas, also by Christians. In a professional context with interlocutors you do not know is the safest choice; ⁧صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ⁩ and ⁧مَسَاءُ الخَيْرِ⁩ They're neutral and they're good everywhere. ⁧مَرْحَبًا⁩ is friendly: use it with colleagues and peers. Formulas with the name of God. ⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ , ⁧إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ and ⁧مَا شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ mā šāʾa llāh The one that God wanted (admiration for something beautiful or successful) are part of the daily language of Arabic speakers of every religion and degree of religiosity. Using them is normal and appreciated; It's not rude. Recognizing them is indispensable: they recur in every conversation and in many texts. The handshake. Among men it is normal and often long. With a woman she lets her hand first: some people, out of religious conviction, do not shake hands with the opposite sex and greet by carrying their right hand to the chest. It is not an offense and should not be commented on. The dialects, just to recognize them. In the daily talk, how are you doing?It changes from country to country. Do not use these forms in exercises: they are used to avoid being distraught.
